architecture-system.scope: Recorded serving release; separate offline history and one release-specific Redis. Other instances and workload internals are in flow/deployment views.

B1.label: Source JSONL → batch ingestion
B1.note: Spark reads the generated source. Full-scale Bronze/Silver and small DP1-DP3 orchestration have separate recorded cohorts.

B2.label: Persisted Parquet datasets
B2.note: Separate Bronze, Silver, Gold, feature and label artifacts reside on shared volumes; this is not a data-lake service or one 100GB training run.

B3.label: Historical retrieval inside the load Pod
B3.note: The load task mounts source/registry state, performs label-free Feast historical retrieval, then joins independent labels by snapshot ID. Layer 2 training expands all five stages.

O1.label: Bounded stage execution
O1.note: Ingest → validate → metadata publication; downstream release requires validate and publication success. Publication itself runs with ALL_DONE to retain failure metadata.

O2.label: Schemas, lineage and assertion outcomes
O2.note: The publisher emits actual stage metadata and validation outcomes to DataHub GMS; a catalog arrow does not imply that all recorded assertions belong to the same execution.

S1.label: Consume Kafka delivery envelopes
S1.note: Flink consumes bounded offsets from the broker and assigns event time before the keyed operators.

S2.label: Finalized windows → retained output → writers
S2.note: The offline writer persists monitoring history in Parquet. The online writer verifies the completed offline release before selecting latest values.

S3.label: Latest monitoring vector via Feast SDK
S3.note: Staged stream CI targets online-serve-jenkins-8 with a separate monitoring project. The original direct push used the shared Docker online service instead.

F1.label: Verified source → separate serving preparation
F1.note: Serving preparation reads its verified feature source and owns a separate registry/project and wall-clock lease. Batch materialization also has its own namespace, expanded in Layer 2 training.

F2.label: Populate serving namespace
F2.note: Refresh materializes eight rolling prediction inputs to the selected serving Redis release and project.

P1.label: Authenticated machine request
P1.note: POST /v1/machines/P-001:predict. Layer 2 prediction expands lookup, rejection and checked return through the gateway.

P2.label: Native online feature lookup and values
P2.note: Feature API reads the release-specific Redis using embedded Feast. It does not read the monitoring project or the earlier Docker Redis.

P3.label: Validated vector → pinned score
P3.note: The API checks schema, both clocks, operating state and exact model lineage; KServe returns score and metadata to the API, which returns through the gateway. Response arrows are explicit in Layer 2.

A1.label: Private user/controller path
A1.note: Browser loopback/IAP and verified upstream HTTPS are distinct hops. Coordinator delegates through the controller; details are expanded in Layer 2 agents.

A2.label: Specialist tool calls and returned facts
A2.note: Only specialists call their allowed MCP tools; coordinator delegates. Retrieval uses features, prediction and per-replica Feast/Milvus knowledge. Drift fetches a consistent bounded cohort (32–200 machines; recorded run: 32) before PSI.

A3.label: Actual machine features and prediction
A3.note: Retrieval calls machine endpoints; Drift MCP obtains a bounded 32–200-machine API cohort (recorded run: 32), then calls the separate Drift API. Layer 2 shows all tool and generation routes.

A4.label: All roles → shared ModelConfig generation route
A4.note: Coordinator, retrieval and drift share llm-d → observer/turn adapter → control → GPU llama.cpp. This subsystem view groups those internals; Layer 2 draws each generation dependency separately.

V1.label: Scoped credential synchronization
V1.note: Gateway credentials are updated by a bounded scoped Vault consumer, not delivered directly to a browser. CI and agent Secret consumers have separate permissions.

C1.label: Gated serving release
C1.note: CI retrieves the selected version, tests and builds, then deploys/verifies/rolls back. Candidate training does not automatically promote the model; OPA is a CI gate, not an admission webhook.

M1.label: Observed generation metrics and traces
M1.note: Agent OTLP follows a separate exact router path to observer and Jaeger, bypassing model selection. Metrics/log/trace stores are separate; Layer 3 maps them to actual runtimes.

O3.label: Six-task RAG orchestration
O3.note: Fetch, chunk, embed, store, validate and publish form a separate governed reference-state pipeline. This is not the telemetry DP1-DP3 cohort.

K1.label: Verified per-replica knowledge snapshot
K1.note: Retrieval MCP copies state per Pod, then uses an embedded encoder, Feast and Milvus Lite. There is no independent Milvus server or direct LLM access to arbitrary reference files.

T1.label: Selected MLflow model bundle and lineage
T1.note: Versioned training publishes data identities and an evaluated candidate. Serving CI separately retrieves the explicitly selected model version and applies release gates; no automatic promotion is implied.

S0.label: Publish replay deliveries to Kafka
S0.note: The replay producer emits arrival-ordered delivery envelopes, including retries and late readings.

flow-batch.scope: DP1-DP3 dependency/data flow; scale cohorts remain separate

B1.label: Read original source files
B1.note: Each raw line is retained with its file and line identity; duplicate exports remain at Bronze.

B2.label: Persist typed raw exports
B2.note: Immutable stage paths and validation reports bind output files to source identities.

B3.label: Read validated Bronze
B3.note: Explicit nullable union schema retains v1/v2 fields; immutable-payload conflicts fail before latest-export selection.

B4.label: Write cleaned warehouse datasets
B4.note: Dedup uses event_id and deterministic created_ts DESC, path ASC, line DESC. Facts join the dimension effective at event time; Parquet joins are not SQL-enforced foreign keys.

B5.label: Read observed telemetry and event histories
B5.note: Feature inputs must satisfy event_ts <= snapshot time and received_ts <= snapshot time; recorded failure history must already be available.

B6.label: Persist label-free rolling history
B6.note: 10-minute rolling sensor features plus age and recorded prior failures form the eight-field prediction vector.

B7.label: Persist targets separately
B7.note: Future truth is used only for labels/censoring. Training load exports exactly id,label and joins after historical retrieval; labels never enter the Feast entity query.

O1.label: Trigger the bounded stage chain
O1.note: The DAG chain controls separate Spark stages and downstream immutable releases. It is not a claim that the full 100GB workload ran through Airflow DP3.

G1.label: Publish stage metadata and outcomes
G1.note: publish_to_datahub uses ALL_DONE to preserve failure outcomes. The next DAG still requires validate and publish to succeed.

flow-stream.scope: Bounded Kafka/Flink replay with staged monitoring feature writes

S1.label: Publish delivery envelopes
S1.note: Retries retain immutable event payloads and vary delivery metadata. Progress markers advance the test event clock explicitly.

S2.label: Consume bounded Kafka offsets
S2.note: Assign event timestamps, then key by immutable event_id. Conflicting payloads fail. A durable SQLite event ledger outlives the processing-time cache.

S3.label: Unique readings → keyed windows
S3.note: Corrected branch uses a 15-minute out-of-orderness watermark and ten-minute tumbling windows. No extra allowed-lateness period is configured.

S4.label: Persist windows and late side output
S4.note: Late rows and absolute keyed windows enter the retained local audit/result store. Post-job snapshot export is explicit; sink checkpoint transactions are outside this milestone.

S5.label: Validated finalized output → bounded writer
S5.note: Writers process retained finalized rows rather than consuming an independent raw Kafka branch. Window identity and payload are checked before intent acknowledgement.

S6.label: OFFLINE push, readback, release pin
S6.note: OfflineStage appends absent keys, reconciles a pending write by readback, and verifies native historical retrieval. It checks that online values did not change.

S7.label: Read verified Parquet and registry
S7.note: OnlineStage verifies offline/registry hashes and source binding, then chooses latest history per machine. It does not independently process raw telemetry.

S8.label: ONLINE push and native readback
S8.note: CI target is online-serve-jenkins-8. Monitoring uses its own Feast project; the earlier direct push instead targeted Docker online:6379.

S9.label: Dedup, expiry and watermark audit records
S9.kind: Flink side output → same SQLite sink
S9.note: Audit records and window/late records share the retained result store. The persistent event ledger is a separate SQLite file owned by the dedup operator.

flow-training.scope: Five-stage versioned KFP path with separate label join and candidate/release boundary

T1.label: Historical feature retrieval
T1.note: get_historical_features receives only machine_id,event_timestamp. Arrival correctness is established by upstream feature construction and source checks, not by passing labels to Feast.

T2.label: Independent labels joined after lookup
T2.note: Export labels as exactly id,label; independently verify snapshot keys; one-to-one joins must preserve every eligible row and label.

T3.label: Typed cohort artifact
T3.note: The artifact describes actual data files; Kubernetes mounts and artifact transport carry the descriptor. The KFP API does not load feature rows into a model itself.

T4.label: Time partitions → Spark training
T4.note: Train-only transformations and validation selection use the frozen protocol. Two executor Pods on one host do not establish multi-host training or HA.

T5.label: Saved selection artifact
T5.note: Validation reloads the actual trained weights and reproduces the validation result rather than trusting only an in-memory score.

T6.label: Verified selection + successful reload receipt
T6.note: registered_evaluate explicitly consumes both selection and verification outputs before holdout evaluation and model registration.

T7.label: Evaluated model, lineage and data version
T7.note: Publication preserves protocol/source/data/run/model identities and registers an evaluated candidate. It does not switch the serving API.

D1.label: Incremental dataset version publication
D1.note: The versioned load publishes only new blobs and references unchanged completed data runs. Publication failure fails the load, preventing unversioned downstream training.

C1.label: Retrieve selected model bundle
C1.note: CI is parameterized by exact SOURCE_COMMIT and MODEL_VERSION. Candidate creation is separate from release approval and deployment gates.

C2.label: Gated Helm deployment and API switch
C2.note: Coverage/mutation/build gates precede stage, A/B checks, atomic Feature API switch and all-machine verification. Failure invokes cleanup/rollback.

R1.label: Source-bound admitted KFP pipeline run
R1.note: Intent, cooldown and replay guards bound candidate submission. The recorded manual probe preserved drift=false; no natural alarm, accuracy-loss proof or automatic serving promotion is implied.

F0.label: Separate bounded batch materialization
F0.note: The batch materialization job uses embedded Feast and writes its project to the Docker Redis also used by original stream push. Neither online path supplies historical training.

flow-prediction.scope: Request/lookup/check/model/checked response; steps do not equal Deployments

U1.label: Authenticated private HTTPS request
U1.note: Local browser/viewer access can use loopback HTTP over IAP; the viewer verifies upstream private-CA TLS and SNI. Layer 3 separates those hops.

U2.label: Forward the allowed machine route
U2.note: The API accepts a known machine ID rather than arbitrary endpoints or caller-supplied model features.

U3.label: In-process native feature read
U3.note: FeatureRuntime.features invokes FeastKServeBackend.fetch; the SDK is not a separate network service.

U4.label: get_online_features by machine ID
U4.note: The backend requests the eight-field feature service and requires PRESENT statuses and the exact requested machine.

U5.label: Native values and event timestamps
U5.note: All fields must be complete and share a valid event timestamp; age is checked against the explicit simulation clock.

U6.label: Validate source, clocks, schema and operating state
U6.note: Check one-hour real preparation lease, ten-minute event/context freshness, arrival availability, exact protocol and stopped state before calling KServe.

U7.label: Fail validation or eligibility
U7.note: Malformed IDs use request validation; unknown machine 404, stopped machine 409 and unavailable/stale/invalid state 503. A post-model provenance failure also becomes 503, not a successful prediction.

U8.label: POST the validated eight-field vector
U8.note: FeastKServeBackend.predict calls /v1/models/iot-pump-failure-v1:predict with instances; the caller cannot choose endpoint/model/headers.

U9.label: Return model prediction and identity
U9.note: Validate exact model metadata against the API pin, score range and decision threshold before accepting the response.

U10.label: Checked API → gateway → client response
U10.note: The response preserves prediction, model and feature_trace, including source/protocol IDs and native timestamps. This is the logical return of the original request, not another public endpoint.

U11.label: Reject invalid model response or provenance
U11.note: A wrong exact model pin, invalid score or inconsistent decision fails after the model call and produces 503. Only a validated model result follows U10 to the client.

flow-agents.scope: Logical controller-routed delegation, specialist tools, all three generation routes and actual private inference chain

A1.label: Dispatch coordinator task
A1.note: The parent session and task are retained by the actual controller. The diagram shows logical role delegation, not direct worker-to-worker TCP connections.

A2.label: Delegate retrieval via controller
A2.note: An Agent tool requests an isolated specialist session through the controller. A direct network call between worker Pods is not implied.

A3.label: Delegate cohort drift via controller
A3.note: The coordinator has a drift Agent tool; the drift specialist owns the assess_feature_drift MCP tool.

G1.label: Coordinator model generation
G1.note: The coordinator references the same default-model-config as both specialists; it does not use a separate hidden LLM backend.

G2.label: Retrieval model generation
G2.note: Generation traffic uses the shared model route; retrieval tool calls use the separate MCP route below.

G3.label: Drift model generation
G3.note: All three individual role connections terminate at the same inference platform. Tool execution and generation are distinct operations.

K1.label: Validate/publish source-bound state; copy per replica
K1.note: The RAG pipeline validates source/chunk/embedding/store identities before release. Init containers copy verified state into each retrieval Pod; there is no standalone Milvus server.

K2.label: Embedded encoder/Feast retrieval
K2.note: KnowledgeReader embeds the question with its pinned CPU encoder and verifies ranked native IDs, text and provenance. State lives inside the consuming Pod, not across a Milvus network service.

K3.label: Ranked chunks and verified citations
K3.note: Results carry source files, document/chunk IDs, revision and snapshot/embedding hashes; content is authored simulator reference material.

M1.label: Retrieval specialist MCP tools and results
M1.note: The specialist tool allowlist contains get_machine_features, predict_failure and search_knowledge. Tool outputs return to this role, distinct from its G2 generation route.

M2.label: Drift specialist MCP tool and result
M2.note: Only assess_feature_drift is exposed to this specialist; input IDs and window are typed and bounded.

M3.label: Machine features and checked prediction
M3.note: Retrieval tools call fixed Feature API machine endpoints and validate their typed identities. The specialist cannot supply arbitrary URLs or rematerialize features.

M4.label: First fetch the bounded 32–200-machine cohort
M4.note: ToolRuntime.drift fetches every requested Feature API record and requires common as_of, preparation, protocol and source hashes before constructing CompareRequest. The request contract accepts 32–200 IDs; the recorded demonstration used 32.

M5.label: Then compare the validated cohort
M5.note: POST /v1/drift:compare consumes typed observations from the actual API records. PSI is deployed; the separate MMD study is not returned by this tool.

G4.label: Observed generation request
G4.note: The llm-d endpoint picker/router forwards generation to the CPU observer. Its turn adapter and model-control container preserve the bounded tool-turn policy before the GPU server.

G5.label: Controlled model request to the fixed GPU backend
G5.note: model-control forwards only to http://iot-model-gpu.iot-llm.svc.cluster.local:8080. Observer/control execute on CPU; llama.cpp uses the GPU worker.

G6.label: Native generated token stream
G6.note: The original model response is forwarded through control/observer; timestamps and tokens are observed without treating animation as telemetry.

G7.label: Return stream through router to requesting role
G7.note: Each generation reply follows its original request to coordinator/retrieval/drift. Exact agent OTLP export is a separate /iot-telemetry/v1/traces route, not model generation.

A4.label: Actual retrieval child result via controller
A4.note: The retained child session includes actual tool outputs and returned text. Acceptance inspects real child status and facts; Completed alone does not prove correctness.

A5.label: Actual drift child result via controller
A5.note: The coordinator preserves returned PSI/reference identities and distinguishes drift from prediction risk or a confirmed pump fault.

A6.label: Coordinator answer through controller/UI
A6.note: The demo separately validates parent, paired real children and MCP facts. External acceptance scripts do not make every completed runtime answer correct automatically.

deployment-runtime.scope: Selected workload groups by actual host/runtime, not a live status inventory or one Deployment per box

U1.label: Local loopback access
U1.note: The browser speaks local loopback HTTP; the IAP SSH process forwards the chosen port. This hop is not labelled public HTTPS.

U2.label: IAP-authenticated SSH forwarding to CPU loopback
U2.note: IAP permits SSH administration; application UIs stay on loopback/private endpoints. No new public application port is implied.

U3.label: Viewer verifies private CA and SNI
U3.note: The bounded host viewer independently authenticates and verifies its HTTPS upstream. It is a distinct process from the NGINX gateway.

U4.label: Allowed private UI/controller route
U4.note: Gateway routes terminate on allowed internal UI/controller services; machine API routes and MCP backends have their own source-bound policies.

D1.label: Bounded PVC mounts into task/driver/executor Pods
D1.note: /workspace source, /ml-data task workspace and /ml-scratch temporary Spark paths are mounted. Versioned load additionally mounts /data-cas. API serving state is copied separately, not this bulk PVC.

D2.label: Docker source/data/scratch mounts
D2.note: Read/write mounts are scoped per job. Service database volumes persist independently; keeping a VM disk is distinct from a running service or current feature lease.

T1.label: Observed private trace export
T1.note: Agent trace requests follow the exact /iot-telemetry/v1/traces bridge through router and observer to Jaeger; model selection is bypassed on this route. Jaeger storage is bounded in memory.

G1.label: CPU control proxy → private GPU service
G1.note: Fixed iot-model-gpu.iot-llm.svc.cluster.local:8080 backend. The GPU Pod is a worker in the same cluster, not a separate public inference endpoint.

G2.label: Generated stream returns through CPU route
G2.note: One GPU and Recreate do not provide zero-downtime rolling updates or physical-host HA. CPU routing/observation and GPU generation remain separate runtime responsibilities.

feature-containers.scope: C4 container slice: historical loading and the recorded feature-serving release

T1.label: Retrieve history inside the KFP load task
T1.note: Feast uses its DuckDB offline provider to query registered Parquet. Labels are loaded separately and joined to retrieved snapshots. Redis is not a training source.

F1.label: Read pinned preparation inputs
F1.note: The serving refresh verifies source and release identity and uses separate serving state before materialization.

S1.label: Verify the offline stage's release before online delivery
S1.note: The online job verifies the retained monitoring release. It does not reuse the ML training FileSource or receive raw Kafka deliveries.

S2.label: Push latest finalized monitoring vectors
S2.note: This is the staged CI path using the release Redis address and its isolated monitoring project. Four stream aggregates do not supply the predictor.

F2.label: Materialize serving features into the selected release
F2.note: The refresh publishes eight rolling feature values to the serving project of online-serve-jenkins-8. The request path subsequently checks an independent preparation lease.

U1.label: Read serving values and native timestamps
U1.note: The in-process lookup selects the serving feature service and project; model calls require current, eligible values and verified source/provenance.

U2.label: Request pinned inference after eligibility checks
U2.note: The result and identity are checked inside Feature API before returning the prediction. See the prediction flow for the fail-closed response branches.

source_encoding: UTF-8 text with CRLF canonicalized to LF
scope: Source-bound views of the recorded system, feature access, dynamic flows and deployment. The serving release and historical Docker Redis are distinct; neither a live readiness check nor a grade.
